Benign_Explanations: Large providers have more combinations and so more rare ones; also uncommon equipment or services, or program-specific modifiers.
Narrative_Caveat: Counts grow with provider size; if the share of unexpected procedure and modifier combinations is also listed, describe them together.
Value_Template: The provider was paid for {value} modifier and procedure combinations that are rare across all providers (peer median {peer_median}; {peer_pct} percentile among peers).
Records_To_Review: Records backing the modifier on sampled lines: trip sheets (origin, destination), delivery tickets, rental vs purchase history (DME), prior authorization file.
Policy_Lever: Modifier edit: allow only valid modifiers for each procedure code; review rare procedure and modifier combinations.
Open_Question: Possible duplicate of rare_proc_proc_mod_count; 'all modifiers together' inferred from key format (RR,N1,-1,-1__E1390). Confirm. Peer_Group: claim category (rarity judged vs all providers).
Change_Note: Plain wording; size caveat; possible duplicate flagged. | v2.1: Cross-reference the LLM cannot act on.
Original_Description: Count Of Rare Procedure Modifiers And Procedure Code Pairs
Purpose: Number of the provider's modifier and procedure code combinations (all modifiers on the line together) that are rare across all providers' paid claims.
Clinical_Context: Number of the provider's modifier and procedure code combinations (all modifiers on the line together) that are rare across all providers' paid claims.

Description: Average of four peer checks on the provider's paid lines: units vs similar-size providers for the code, units vs all providers for the code, code mix, and diagnosis mix. Near 0 is typical.
Suspicious_Pattern: Concerning when well above 0: the provider's paid procedures look unusual on several checks at once compared with peers in the same category.
Benign_Explanations: Specialty or niche service mix, small number of claims, a few unusual patients.
Narrative_Caveat: A summary of other measures; it does not say which part is unusual. Narrate the specific measures instead.
Value_Template: The provider's combined reading across four procedure checks was {value}, where 0 is typical of peers (peer median {peer_median}; {peer_pct} percentile among peers).
Records_To_Review: Paid lines for the provider's top procedure codes with units and diagnoses, compared with peer claims for the same codes.
Policy_Lever: none
Open_Question: Confirm level (computed per claim line, then rolled up to provider how?) and the exact peer group for each of the four parts. Peer_Group defaulted to same claim category.
Change_Note: Removed z-score/composite wording; made it a context summary since it cannot explain itself.
Original_Description: Numeric composite z-score averaging four procedure-related z-scores (volume, procedure proportion, global quantity, diagnosis proportion)
Derivation (col G): mean(axis=1) of procedure_volume_zscore, proccodeproportionzscore, global_procedure_zscore, diagcodeproportionzscore.
Purpose: Average of four peer checks on the provider's paid lines: units vs similar-size providers for the code, units vs all providers for the code, code mix, and diagnosis mix. Near 0 is typical.
Clinical_Context: Average of four peer checks on the provider's paid lines: units vs similar-size providers for the code, units vs all providers for the code, code mix, and diagnosis mix. Near 0 is typical.

Description: Average number of paid visits a patient had with this provider in a month, averaged across the provider's patients and months.
Suspicious_Pattern: Concerning when patients are seen many more times a month than at peer providers, consistent with excessive visits.
Benign_Explanations: Intensive treatment plans, new treatment episodes, dialysis transport (about 13 round trips a month), small patient count.
Narrative_Caveat: Not meaningful for nursing homes or residential facilities, which are paid for every day a member stays.
Value_Template: The provider's patients averaged {value} paid visits per month with this provider (peer median {peer_median}; {peer_pct} percentile among peers).
Records_To_Review: Member visit history by month, sign-in sheets or progress notes for top members, same-day claims for those members across all providers.
Policy_Lever: Frequency edit: cap paid visits per member per month for the code; review members above the cap.
Applies_To: All except NURSING HOME; BH RESIDENTIAL TREATMENT
Open_Question: Confirm whether this is averaged over patient-months, or total visits to the provider per month (not per patient).
Change_Note: Stated per-patient monthly reading; excluded daily-paid facilities; paired with monthly_provider_visit_count via Concept_Group. | v2.1: Delivery or confirmation wording.

Description: Average number of paid claim lines per distinct patient over the review period (total paid claim lines divided by the number of patients).
Suspicious_Pattern: Concerning when each patient generates many more paid lines than at peers, consistent with unbundling (one service split into several lines) or excessive visits.
Benign_Explanations: Long-term or residential patients with daily lines, complex chronic patients, a few patients in long treatment.

Original_Description: Average number of claim lines per unique patient for this provider
Purpose: Average number of paid claim lines per distinct patient over the review period (total paid claim lines divided by the number of patients).
Clinical_Context: Average number of paid claim lines per distinct patient over the review period (total paid claim lines divided by the number of patients).

Description: Total dollars paid to the transport provider divided by its total paid miles, compared with other transport providers.
Suspicious_Pattern: Concerning when far from peers: low can mean paid miles run high relative to trips; high can mean costlier vehicle codes or many base and wait charges on short trips.
Benign_Explanations: High: short urban trips, wheelchair or stretcher vans, frequent waits. Low: mostly long rural or reservation trips where miles outweigh base charges.
Narrative_Caveat: Two-sided: say which pattern applies only if paid miles per trip is also listed; otherwise say it differs from peers.
Value_Template: The provider was paid {value} per paid mile across its trips (peer median {peer_median}; {peer_pct} percentile among peers).
Records_To_Review: Paid trip detail with codes, vehicle type and miles; trip sheets and dispatch records; AHCCCS NEMT fee schedule for those vehicle types.
Policy_Lever: Rate audit: compare paid per mile with fee schedule by vehicle type; edit on mileage units per trip.
Open_Question: Confirm whether total payments include base, wait-time and mileage codes, or mileage codes only. PER_MILE_PROC_CDS includes T2005, a per-trip stretcher van code; if this feature uses that list, trips are counted as miles.
Change_Note: Made direction two-sided and conditional; replaced 'billed distance' with paid miles. | v2.1: Cross-reference the LLM cannot act on; Scheme name outside KNOWN_SCHEMES.
Original_Description: Average payment amount per mile of billed distance for this NEMT provider
Purpose: Total dollars paid to the transport provider divided by its total paid miles, compared with other transport providers.

Description: Average total dollars paid to the provider per distinct patient over the review period, compared with peers in the same category.
Suspicious_Pattern: Concerning when each patient brings in far more payment than at peers, consistent with excessive visits or upcoding.
Benign_Explanations: Sicker or long-stay patients, costly equipment or specialty services, a small number of patients.
Narrative_Caveat: Unstable when the provider has few patients; compare within the same category only.
Value_Template: The provider was paid an average of {value} per patient (peer median {peer_median}; {peer_pct} percentile among peers).
Records_To_Review: Paid claims for the highest-paid members (services and units by date); progress notes or delivery records for a sample.
Policy_Lever: Audit: review members with the highest paid totals; per-member spending alert by category.

Suspicious_Pattern: Concerning when the provider's costly services sit at the very top of the cost range more than peers, consistent with upcoding to the costliest codes.
Benign_Explanations: Specialty services where top-cost codes are routine (power wheelchairs, complex DME, specialized BH programs).
Narrative_Caveat: Covers only costly codes, so values sit near the top of the scale and small gaps look large; says how costly, not how many.

Records_To_Review: Paid lines for the provider's high-cost codes with modifiers and units; prior authorization file; clinical record review for a sample.

Description: Average dollars paid per paid claim line (total paid divided by number of paid claim lines), compared with peers in the same category.
Suspicious_Pattern: Concerning when each paid line pays much more than at peers for similar services, consistent with upcoding or extra units on each line.
Benign_Explanations: Costly service mix (power mobility, specialty DME), many units per line by design, facility per-day lines.
Narrative_Caveat: Driven by service mix; compare within the same category only.
Value_Template: The provider was paid an average of {value} per paid claim line (peer median {peer_median}; {peer_pct} percentile among peers).
Records_To_Review: Highest-paid claim lines with codes, modifiers and units; fee schedule rates for those codes; supporting service records for a sample.

Description: Average total dollars paid to the transport provider per distinct patient over the review period, compared with other transport providers.
Suspicious_Pattern: Concerning when each rider brings in far more payment than at peer transport providers, consistent with mileage inflation (miles or wait time) or phantom billing (trips).
Benign_Explanations: Dialysis riders (about 3 round trips a week), long rural trips, a small number of riders with frequent needs.
Narrative_Caveat: Unstable with few riders; it rises with trips per patient and miles per trip.
Value_Template: The provider was paid an average of {value} per rider for transport (peer median {peer_median}; {peer_pct} percentile among peers).
Records_To_Review: Trip history for top-paid riders: trip sheets, driver logs, GPS or odometer data, and same-day medical claims for those riders.

Description: Average number of paid units (time units, miles, or items, depending on the code) on each paid claim line, looked at across the provider's patients.
Suspicious_Pattern: Concerning when lines carry far more units than peers for the same codes, consistent with frequency abuse or phantom billing.
Benign_Explanations: Long sessions paid in small time units, monthly supply lines, long trips paid per mile.
Narrative_Caveat: Unit size differs by code (minutes, miles, items); compare only within similar services.

Records_To_Review: Lines with the most units (code, unit size, dates); progress notes with session times, trip sheets, or delivery tickets to match units.

Description: Average total paid units of service per distinct patient over the review period, for this provider.

Benign_Explanations: Patients who need several specialists or vendors; patients who change providers during the period.

Suspicious_Pattern: Concerning when time-based units paid for one patient on one day add up to more hours than peers show or than fit in a day, consistent with impossible day billing.
Benign_Explanations: Long treatment days (day programs, residential services), several items delivered at once, long trips.

Original_Description: Average number of trips billed per day the provider was actively billing

Description: Average number of paid trips per distinct patient for the transport provider over the review period, compared with other transport providers.
Suspicious_Pattern: Concerning when riders are paid for many more trips than at peers, especially without a same-day medical visit, consistent with phantom billing or excessive visits.
Benign_Explanations: Dialysis (about 3 round trips a week), chemotherapy, BH day programs, recurring therapy visits.

Description: Average paid wait-time units per trip (code T2007; 1 unit = 30 minutes) across the provider's paid trips. A value of 2 means about 1 hour of paid waiting per trip.
Suspicious_Pattern: Concerning when well above peers, or above 4 units (2 hours) per trip on average, consistent with mileage inflation (which covers wait-time quantities).
Benign_Explanations: Long dialysis or procedure appointments where the driver waits; rural trips where driving back empty is impractical.
Narrative_Caveat: Averages in trips with no wait, so a few very long waits can hide. AHCCCS fee-for-service pays no wait time on one-way trips or trips of 10 miles or less.
Value_Template: The provider was paid an average of {value} wait-time units per trip (peer median {peer_median}; {peer_pct} percentile among peers).
Records_To_Review: Trips with paid T2007 units: trip sheets with pickup, drop-off and return times, appointment times from the medical claim, GPS data.
Policy_Lever: Edit: cap T2007 units per trip; require appointment times for waits over 4 units (2 hours).

Original_Description: Average number of wait-time units (15-min increments) billed per transport trip
Purpose: Average paid wait-time units per trip (code T2007; 1 unit = 30 minutes) across the provider's paid trips. A value of 2 means about 1 hour of paid waiting per trip.
Clinical_Context: Average paid wait-time units per trip (code T2007; 1 unit = 30 minutes) across the provider's paid trips. A value of 2 means about 1 hour of paid waiting per trip.

Description: Change in the provider's total paid dollars from the prior quarter to the current quarter, as a share of the prior quarter (0.5 = 50% more paid).
Suspicious_Pattern: Concerning when payments jump sharply in one quarter without a matching rise in patients.
Benign_Explanations: New provider or location, new contract or service line, delayed claims paid in a batch, a low prior quarter.
Narrative_Caveat: Unstable when the prior quarter was small (new providers): $500 to $5,000 shows as 900% growth.
Value_Template: The provider's paid dollars changed by {value} from the prior quarter to the current quarter (0.5 = 50% more; -0.5 = 50% less).
Records_To_Review: Paid amounts by month and code for both quarters, new members or codes behind the rise, enrollment file for new locations or owners.
Policy_Lever: Monitoring rule: prepayment review when a provider's quarterly paid amount jumps past a set multiple.

Change_Note: Renamed in plain words as payment growth; added small-base instability caveat. | v2.1: Scheme name outside KNOWN_SCHEMES.
Original_Description: Quarter-over-quarter change in total payments for this provider

Purpose: Change in the provider's total paid dollars from the prior quarter to the current quarter, as a share of the prior quarter (0.5 = 50% more paid).

Benign_Explanations: Falls automatically as claim volume grows; single-service providers (one DME item, one trip type) are narrow by nature.
Narrative_Caveat: Tied to size: large providers score low by arithmetic alone. Do not cite alone; mention it only if claim volume measures are also listed.

Description: Number of paid facility claims with leave-of-absence revenue codes (018X): days the bed was held while the resident was away, such as a home visit (0183) or hospital stay (0185).
Suspicious_Pattern: Concerning when leave days are paid far more often than at peer facilities, past the yearly leave-day limits, or on dates another facility was also paid for the resident.

Replacement: Patients who see only this provider
Description: Share of the provider's patients who had no paid services from any other provider of the same type during the review period.

Benign_Explanations: Rural sole provider, tribal or IHS-linked service, specialty niche, or strong patient loyalty.
Narrative_Caveat: Weigh against rural or metro location; a rural sole provider looks the same.

Replacement: Days with 3 or more trips for one patient
Description: Share of the transport provider's active days on which a single patient had 3 or more paid trips.
Suspicious_Pattern: Concerning when far more common than for peers: extra paid trips for the same patient on one day, consistent with duplicate billing or unbundling.
Benign_Explanations: Several appointments in one day, a pharmacy stop after a visit, hospital discharge plus follow-up, or each leg paid as its own claim.

Replacement: Trip days with a ride there and a ride back
Description: Share of the transport provider's trip days where the same patient had both a ride there and a ride back paid on the same day.
Suspicious_Pattern: Concerning when far from peers: very low (many one-way rides, possibly round trips split across providers) or near 100% where peers are lower (return rides paid by default).
Benign_Explanations: Patient got another ride home, was admitted to the hospital, or a different company did the return trip.
Narrative_Caveat: Most medical trips are round trips, so a high share is usually normal; it matters only when far above peers.
Value_Template: {value} of the provider's trip days had both a paid ride there and a paid ride back for the same patient (peer median {peer_median}; provider at the {peer_pct} percentile).
Records_To_Review: Trip sheets and dispatch records for one-way trips; return trips paid to other transport providers that day; hospital admission claims.
Policy_Lever: Audit: match one-way trips to return trips paid to other providers the same day; check for split round trips.
Open_Question: Matched on member and service date only: confirm it checks direction (there and back) rather than any 2 trips on one day.

Description: Share of the facility's paid claims with subacute revenue codes. In AHCCCS, 0191 to 0193 (subacute Levels 1 to 3) are the usual nursing home day codes, so most claims carry one.
Suspicious_Pattern: Context only: most paid nursing home days carry these codes, so a high share is normal; a low share mostly reflects leave-day claims or other coding.
Benign_Explanations: Facilities with many leave or hospital bed-hold days (paid on separate claims) show lower shares; specialized units are paid more higher-level days.
Narrative_Caveat: Do not call a high share unusual or a sign of higher-level care: most AHCCCS nursing home days are paid under these codes.
Value_Template: {value} of the facility's paid claims carried subacute (0191 to 0193) revenue codes, the usual nursing home day codes (peer median {peer_median}; provider at the {peer_pct} percentile).

Clinical_Context: Share of the facility's paid claims with subacute revenue codes. In AHCCCS, 0191 to 0193 (subacute Levels 1 to 3) are the usual nursing home day codes, so most claims carry one.

Replacement: Trips with no same-day medical visit
Description: Share of the transport provider's paid trips where no paid medical claim from any provider was found for the same patient on the same day.
Suspicious_Pattern: Concerning when far above peers: many paid rides with no paid visit on record to show where the patient went; consistent with phantom billing.
Benign_Explanations: Visit paid by Medicare or another payer, IHS/638 visits not in this data, monthly or date-span destination claims (dialysis), late claims, or covered stops.
Narrative_Caveat: Based on matching same-day claims: describe it as no matching paid medical claim found, which does not show whether the trip took place.
Value_Template: {value} of the provider's paid trips had no matching paid medical claim for the member that day (peer median {peer_median}; provider at the {peer_pct} percentile).
Records_To_Review: Trip sheets and GPS with destination type (FFS has not covered trips to community support programs since 7/1/2022); same-day claims across all payers.
Policy_Lever: Prepayment edit: require a same-day destination claim or verified trip log (pickup, drop-off, appointment) to pay.

Clinical_Context: Share of the transport provider's paid trips where no paid medical claim from any provider was found for the same patient on the same day.

Description: Share of the transport provider's paid trips with more than 50 paid miles, compared with other transport providers.
Suspicious_Pattern: Concerning when long trips are far more common than for peers serving similar areas; consistent with mileage inflation.
Benign_Explanations: Rural or reservation patients, trips to specialty centers in Phoenix or Tucson, or dialysis far from home.
Narrative_Caveat: AHCCCS FFS requires prior authorization for trips over 100 miles (IHS/638 transport exempt). This share alone cannot show trips clustering under 100.

Records_To_Review: Trip sheets, GPS or odometer data; mapped pickup-to-destination miles; prior authorization file (AHCCCS FFS: trips over 100 miles; IHS/638 transport exempt).
Policy_Lever: Edit: compare paid miles with mapped route miles; review trips of 90 to 100 miles that stay under the PA cutoff.
Open_Question: AHCCCS sources differ: NEMT FAQ says roundtrips over 100 miles need PA; FFS manual Ch.14 (rev 07/31/2026) says trips over 100 miles. Confirm which, and if distance is per leg. PER_MILE_PROC_CDS includes T2005, a per-trip stretcher van code; if this feature uses that list, trips are counted as miles.

Purpose: Share of the transport provider's paid trips with more than 50 paid miles, compared with other transport providers.
Clinical_Context: Share of the transport provider's paid trips with more than 50 paid miles, compared with other transport providers.

Description: Share of the transport provider's paid trips with less than 1 paid mile. Each such trip still earns a base trip payment.
Suspicious_Pattern: Concerning when far above peers: many very short trips each paid a base rate, consistent with unbundling (one ride split into several paid trips) or phantom billing.
Benign_Explanations: Dense urban areas, moves between buildings on a medical campus, or wheelchair and stretcher patients who cannot walk short distances.
Narrative_Caveat: Does not show whether short trips run back to back for the same patient, which is what would suggest split trips.

Clinical_Context: Share of the transport provider's paid trips with less than 1 paid mile. Each such trip still earns a base trip payment.

Replacement: Share of claims that are paid wait time
Description: Share of the transport provider's paid claims that are for wait time (code T2007, paid in 30-minute units), compared with other transport providers.
Suspicious_Pattern: Concerning when far above peers, most of all on one-way trips or trips of 10 miles or less, where AHCCCS fee-for-service does not pay wait time.
Benign_Explanations: Long appointments such as dialysis or chemotherapy, rural trips where the driver must wait, or stretcher patients.
Narrative_Caveat: Do not suggest a problem unless the share of payments from wait time or paid wait time per trip is also listed and unusual.
Value_Template: {value} of the provider's paid claims were for wait time (T2007) (peer median {peer_median}; provider at the {peer_pct} percentile).
Records_To_Review: Driver logs and dispatch records with arrival and pickup times; GPS data; appointment length from the member's same-day medical claim.
Policy_Lever: Edit (FFS Ch.14): no T2007 on one-way trips, waits under 30 min, or trips 10 miles or less; one member per shared ride.

Clinical_Context: Share of the transport provider's paid claims that are for wait time (code T2007, paid in 30-minute units), compared with other transport providers.

Description: Share of the transport provider's paid trips with a service date on a Saturday or Sunday, compared with other transport providers.
Suspicious_Pattern: Concerning when far above peers for riders whose visits are usually on weekdays; worth matching weekend trips to same-day medical claims.

Replacement: Concentration on a few procedure codes

Benign_Explanations: Single-service providers, such as a dialysis-only transport company or an oxygen supplier, normally use very few codes.
Narrative_Caveat: Measures concentration, not cost; do not suggest upcoding unless high-cost code measures are also listed and unusual.

Replacement: Codes paid over the frequency limit
Description: Share of the provider's procedure codes where paid services went over the policy frequency limit (how often the code may be paid in a set time).
Suspicious_Pattern: Concerning when many of the provider's codes were paid over frequency limits: a repeated pattern, and a sign the limit is not enforced by a claim edit.

Clinical_Context: Share of the provider's procedure codes where paid services went over the policy frequency limit (how often the code may be paid in a set time).
